Hi Anna — great to hear you're ready to start. Short answer: yes, Redwood can coordinate the ingest and we recommend a hybrid presign + small-batch push approach. High-level plan below.

Plan (proposal):
- Roadmap: kickoff workshop (1 hour) this week -> pilot import (subset 200 files) -> full seeding in controlled waves.
- Upload pattern: generate presigned S3 links for large artifacts (>5MB); for small docs batch via Whistic API in 25–50 item chunks.
- Throttling guidance: target 2 concurrent upload worker processes per region with 500ms inter-request spacing to stay under typical Whistic rate limits. We’ll add exponential backoff (base 1s, max 32s) for 429/5xx.
- Integrity: Redwood will validate checksums and post an ingestion summary CSV back to you after each wave.

Action items:
- Anna: share a 30–50 file sample manifest (names + sizes + desired tags).
- Ben: I’m looping you for SOW/ops notes and to coordinate timing.
- Laura and Rafael: please review the presign window suggestion below and confirm if this approach meets our security controls.

Anna / team — thanks for the heads-up. Quick security checklist and controls confirmation for the proposed pattern below.

Security checklist (redwood -> prospectco onboarding):
- Presign policy: default 8-hour expiry, support parameterized TTL per wave (1h/4h/8h). Presign URLs are single-use (we will rotate keys if reissue is requested).
- Audit logging: platform will emit an upload event for each presign usage including: actor email, timestamp, checksum (sha256), object key stub, and presign token id. Logs will be retained for 365 days for onboarding runs.
- Encryption: uploaded objects must be SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS depending on ProspectCo preference; we support both. Please indicate preferred KMS alias if you want SSE-KMS.
- Integrity checks: Redwood will verify sha256 after upload; failed checksum attempts will retry with exponential backoff and escalate after 3 failures.
- Minimal retention during transit: we do not persist file bodies on Redwood; only metadata and checksums.

Operational notes:
- Pilot wave: 200 files, 2 workers/region, 30s per-file rolling window to avoid spikes.
- Full waves: increase workers to 6 and stagger by tag groups (security, privacy, infra) to make ticketing granular.

Deliverables before kickoff:
1) Prospective sample manifest (CSV) with file size column and tag column (Anna).
2) KMS alias or preference for encryption mode (ProspectCo).
3) Redwood SOW draft for onboarding (Ben).
4) Workshop agenda + calendar invite (Stephanie).

Attachments: SOC2_Controls_Summary.pdf (summary of which SOC2 sections map to SIG/CAIQ fields)

If all agree, we'll schedule the workshop for Thu 30 Jun 2027 at 09:00 PT — I’ll be on the call to walk through the audit trail and presign lifecycle.
